rows.author: I044;I037;I033;C105;I039;H046;G017;
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PROHIBITING OBSTRUCTION AND SLOWDOWN OF TRAFFIC WHILE UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF ROAD RAGE, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines “Road Rage” as a person´s anger or violent behaviour that is usually caused by another person´s bad driving or the stress of being in heavy traffic; and is expressed in aggressive or violent behaviour, thus causing the total or partial obstruction or slowdown of vehicular traffic and endangering the lives and safety of the public.

Provides penalties from Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) to Twenty Thousand Pesos (P20,000.00) plus the revocation of the driver´s license of the offending driver.

Mandates the owner of CCTV systems, cameras, mobile phones or similar equipment, which was used to capture the actual act of road rage, to produce a hardcopy of the footage or effect a transfer thereof to responding traffic enforcers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A UNIVERSAL NEWBORN HEARING SCREENING PROGRAM FOR THE PREVENTION, EARLY DIAGNOSIS AND INTERVENTION OF HEARING LOSS AMONG CHILDREN
rows.abstract:
Provides that all babies born in Philippine hospitals, upon the consent of parents or legal guardians, shall be made to undergo newborn hearing loss screening before discharge. Babies who are not born in hospitals should be screened within the first three (3) months of life.

States that a parent or legal guardian may refuse hearing loss screening on the grounds of religious beliefs but shall acknowledge in writing that they have been informed of their responsibility to perform said screening.   

Mandates the DOH to require health institutions to provide hearing loss screening services as a condition of licensure. It shall also establish an Advisory Committee on Newborn Hearing Screening to facilitate interagency coordination and the cooperation of private sector and professional associations in policy development, technology development, enforcement monitoring, data banking and training.
rows.alias_name: “Universal Newborn Hearing Screening and Intervention Act.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I091;
rows.title_full: AN ACT RECLASSIFYING THE SALARY AND QUALIFICATIONS OF CERTAIN EMPLOYEES IN THE JUDICIARY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to reclassify and increase the salaries of 18 positions in the Judiciary which shall be commensurate to their merits, qualifications and amount of works that they perform. 

States that increasing the salaries of these court personnel will enable them to focus on their work and contribute in the speedy and efficient administration of justice in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 7432, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NOS. 9994, 9257 AND 10645 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Grants senior citizens exemption from all parking fees and local “colorcoding” or number blocking of vehicles.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SENIOR CITIZENS since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE INTEGRATION OF BASIC COMPUTER LITERACY AND ADVANCED COMPUTER EDUCATION AS ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS IN THE CURRICULA OF GRADES 3 TO 12 OF THE \"K TO 12\" (K-12) EDUCATIONAL SYSTEM IN ALL PUBLIC SCHOOLS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides for the following rules and regulations: 1.) adoption of a uniform syllabus for every applicable computer literacy program commensurate to the grade levels of the “K-12” program; 2.) training of qualified members of the school faculty; 3.) establishment of at least one (1) computer laboratory for every school; 4.) acquisition of desktop computers and peripherals primarily through donation; 5.) necessary maintenance of computers and peripherals acquired; 6.) acquisition and maintenance of WIFI network connectivity for the computer laboratory; and 7.) commencement of the entire program, which is at the start of the school year immediately following the effectivity of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PENSION AND HEALTH BENEFITS TO COMFORT WOMEN, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Tasks the National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women (NCRFW) to determine the authenticity of the claims and identifies of comfort women with the assistance of the various accredited cause-oriented women´s group. 

Mandates the PVAO to provide Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000.00) monthly pension for comfort women and the Philhealth to provide free full medical insurance to comfort women as may be determine by the NCRFW.
rows.alias_name: “The Comfort Women Compensation and Benefit Act.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AN INCREASE IN THE SALARY OF, AND ADDITIONAL INCENTIVES FOR, GOVERNMENT PHYSICIANS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFORE
rows.abstract: Seeks to adjust the salary of Government Physician to Salary Grade 24 and provide those who have rendered at least three (3) years of government service an annual loyalty pay equivalent to 75% of the one (1) month of their prevailing salary.  Government doctors who have rendered at least five (5) years of continuous service shall be entitled to an educational grant for any medical course and training whether locally or internationally. Provides further, for transportation, representation, food, and medical allowances for public doctors that are assigned to isolated, depressed, or conflict-torn areas.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SOLAR ENERGY DEVELOPMENT CENTER AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Aims to establish the Solar Energy Development Center  that shall serve as the leading institution concerned with the research on solar energy; the development of technologies needed for the utilization of solar energy; the implementation of government program on the allocation, distribution, and sale of solar energy; and the promotion of the use, research, and introduction of solar energy-related technologies to the market.
rows.status: Referred to Stakeholders on 2018-10-15

rows.abstract: Seeks to grant hazard pay without tax to Judges of the Metropolitan Trial Court in recognition of their hard work and prompt action on criminal cases that need to be resolved.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2018-10-02

rows.author: I088;I089;I077;I079;I091;I103;I104;I087;I102;I085;I011;I092;I036;C009;H015;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING FOR SINGLE PARTY CONSENSUAL RECORDING IN LAW ENFORCEMENT
rows.abstract: Authorizes a law enforcement officer to record an oral communication to which the officer or a person under the supervision of the officer is a party. Such recording shall not be admissible to court unless it is proven that the recording is free from any alterations and shall contain the recitation of the circumstances including the identity of the person making the recording, the date, time and place where the recording is made, the person/s subject of the recording, and the offense for which the recording is being made.
rows.alias_name: “Consensual Recording for Law Enforcement Act of 2018.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2018-10-03

rows.author: D095;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10068 OR THE ORGANIC AGRICULTURE ACT OF 2010
rows.abstract:
Aims to further promote, propagate, develop and implement the organic farming and other sustainable agriculture practices in the country that will enrich the fertility of the soil, increase farm productivity and farmer´s income and promote food self sufficiency.

Institutionalizes the Participatory Guarantee system (PGS) to help small organic farmers attain the organic certification they need to compete in local and global markets.

Includes three (3) representatives from the private sector or agribusiness firms involved in organic agriculture for the last three years in the composition of the National Organic Agriculture Board (NOAB) to increase organic expertise and achieve a more balanced public-private partnership on the NOAB.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2018-10-03

rows.author: G017;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE BARANGAYS THROUGH SUPPORT FOR BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND VOLUNTEER WORKERS
rows.abstract: Seeks to provide additional benefits to Barangay officials and volunteer workers by increasing their honorariums and granting them additional incentives and benefits like retirement benefits, training and workshops, and free legal service to properly compensate and equip barangay officials with necessary training and enable them to efficiently and effectively carry out their mandated tasks.
rows.alias_name: “Barangay Officials and Volunteer Workers Incentives and Benefits Act of 2018.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-10-03

rows.author: G017;
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO ALL BARANGAY OFFICIALS WHO HAVE RENDERED AT LEAST 3 (THREE) TERMS OF CONTINUOUS SERVICE AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Grants lump sum retirement benefits to elected barangay officials equivalent to one and a half (1 Â½ ) month of his/her last honorium for every year of service which shall be taken form the Barangay Retirement Fund. 

Prohibits barangay officials who were convicted of a crime or have pending criminal or administrative cases filed against them from availing the said retirement benefits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-10-03

rows.abstract: Seeks to amend Section 11 of RA No. 10410 by increasing the amount to be contributed by the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation from Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500,000,000.00) to One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000.00) per year for another five (5) years to fund the establishment of National Child Development Centers and the conversion of existing Day Care Centers into Child Development Centers in various local government units to be directly remitted in four (4) quarterly installments to a special account of the EDDC Council.

rows.author: C046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA FOR THE STATISTICAL, CIVIL REGISTRATION AND PHILIPPINE IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM WORKERS OF THE PHILIPPINES, AUTHORIZING THE COLLECTION AND APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to ensure a reservoir of talent who are adequately provided with compensation and benefits at par with the private sector that shall address the issues confronting the human resources of the statistical, civil registration and PhilSys sectors.

Mandates the creation of additional Deputy National Statisticians, transfer of the administrative and operations management, control and supervision of the Local Civil Registrars and their staff from the LGUs to PSA and the officials and employees of which shall be transferred to and absorbed by the Local Statistics Office to be established in each City and Municipality, and establishment of the Philippine Statistics AttachÃ© in each Philippine Embassy and Consular Office or clusters.

Mandates the Local Chief Executives concerned to allocate and donate adequate lots or areas for the construction of buildings and structures, and sustained operations of the PSA Field Offices in their respective Municipality, City, Provincial or regional government centers; and the DBM and Congress to ensure sufficient amounts for the procurement of buildings, equipment facilities and materials for the PSA Filed Offices and Local Statistics Office.
rows.alias_name: “Magna Carta for the Statistical, Civil Registration and Philippine Identification System Workers
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2018-10-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE MANDATORY COMPLIANCE BY ALL MOTORCYCLE RIDERS AND OPERATORS TO AUTOMATICALLY TURN ON AND RIDE WITH THEIR HEADLIGHTS ON AT ALL HOURS OF THE DAY AND NIGHT ON ALL ROADS
rows.title_short: Requiring The Mandatory Compliance By All Motorcycle Riders And Operators To Automatically Turn On And Ride With Their Headlights On At All Hours Of The Day And Night On All Roads
rows.abstract: Requires all motorcycle manufactures, assemblers and distributors to ensure that all motorcycles are equipped with an automatic headlights on system, mechanism or device before its sale or distribution; Prohibits the registration and succeeding renewal of registration of motorcycles without the required automatic headlights system; Provides penalties and fines for the violation of this Act; Mandates the LTO, in coordination with the Philippine Information Agency, the DepEd and other private agencies and organizations concerned to conduct nationwide information education and communication campaign that shall stress and promote the public safety awareness in observance of and compliance with this Act.
rows.alias_name: “Mandatory Automatic Headlights On for Motorcycles Act.”
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2018-11-26, transmitted to the Senate on 2018-11-27 and received by the Senate on 2018-11-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT OF FOREIGN NATIONALS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 40, 41 AND 42 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES\"
rows.title_short: Strengthening The Regulation Of Employment Of Foreign Nationals, Amending For The Purpose Articles 40, 41 And 42 Of Presidential Decree No. 442, As Amended, Otherwise Known As The \" Labor Code Of The Philippines \"
rows.abstract:
Mandates that ALL NON-RESIDENT FOREIGN NATIONALS seeking employment in the Philippines shall obtain an employment permit from the Department of Labor and Employment and shall be subjected to a Labor Market Test based on non-availability of qualified and willing Filipino nationals.

States that foreign nationals issued employment permits shall transfer technology to Filipino understudies within a prescribed period.

Prohibits foreign national issued an employment permit to transfer to another job or change employer without prior approval of the Secretary of Labor and Employment.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES (SUCs) TO PREPARE AND IMPLEMENT A LAND USE DEVELOPMENT AND INFRASTRUCTURE PLAN THAT SHALL INCLUDE THE CONSTRUCTION OF DORMITORIES FOR STUDENTS AND HOUSING SITES FOR EMPLOYEES
rows.title_short: Requiring State Universities And Colleges ( S U Cs ) To Prepare And Implement A Land Use Development And Infrastructure Plan That Shall Include The Construction Of Dormitories For Students And Housing Sites For Employees
rows.abstract:
Requires SUCs  to follow the required LUDIP on all land use or infrastructure projects which shall be submitted to the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) within two (2) years after approval of this Act and to be updated periodically as the need arises.

Mandates all government departments, agencies, offices, and instrumentalities to extend all possible assistance and cooperation to the SUCs in the preparation of their LUDIP.

Provides for the coverage of LUDIP which includes the following, among others: detailed geographical and survey site occupied by the SUCs; detailed description and survey site intended for dormitories for students and housing sites for employees; design and estimated cost of construction, operation, maintenance of other infrastructure needs of the SUCs; and financial plan, which shall include the conduct and submission of feasibility studies, sources of funds and other financial schemes or arrangements.

rows.title_short: Providing For The Revised Corporation Code Of The Philippines
rows.abstract:
Provides for a Revised Corporation Code based on international best practices and standards to address and meet the needs and realities of business in the Philippines; encourage new businesses, deter corporate fraud and abuse, strengthen good corporate governance and rationalize the authority of the Security and Exchange Commission.

Seeks to allow the corporation to have perpetual life existence; accept electronic filing with the SEC, thereby contributing to the ease of doing business; permit stockholders to vote remotely, at the option of the corporation; allow the establishment of one-person corporations; and require the SEC to notify and coordinate with the appropriate government agency prior to the suspension or revocation of the certificate of incorporation of companies under the agency´s special regulatory jurisdiction.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4200, ENTITLED, \"AN ACT TO PROHIBIT AND PENALIZE WIRE TAPPING AND OTHER RELATED VIOLATIONS OF THE PRIVACY OF COMMUNICATION\"
rows.title_short: Amending Republic Act No. 4200, Entitled \" An Act To Prohibit And Penalize Wire Tapping And Other Related Violations Of The Privacy Of Communication, And For Other Purposes\"
rows.abstract:
Declares it unlawful for any person, not being authorized by any party to any ORAL, WIRE, RADIO, DIGITAL OR ELECTRONIC private communication, to tap, intercept or record such communication WITH THE USE OF ANY ELECTRONIC, MECHANICAL, DIGITAL OR ANALOG PHONE SYSTEM, OR SIMILAR DEVICES.

Includes the crimes or offenses in the following as addition to those enumerated under Section 3 of RA 4200, namely: (1) Violation of RA 9165, or the “Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002”, as amended; (2) Coup d´etat, Conspiracy and Proposal to Commit Coup d´etat, Robbery in Band as defined and penalized by Articles 294, 295, 296, 299 and 302 of the Revised Penal Code; (3) Presidential Decree No. 532, otherwise known as the “Anti-Piracy and Anti-Highway Robbery Law of 1974; (4) Violation of RA 3019, or the “Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act”; (7) Syndicated Illegal recruitment as defined and punished under RA 8042; and, (6) Violation of RA 9160, otherwise known as the “Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2001,” as amended.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2018-11-26, transmitted to the Senate on 2018-11-27 and received by the Senate on 2018-11-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND EXPANDING THE PROFESSIONAL RIGHTS AND WORK INCENTIVES OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4670, TO BE KNOWN AS THE EXPANDED MAGNA CARTA FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Proposes several amendments to R.A. No. 4670 (Magna Carta for Public School Teachers) as regards to: a. recruitment, selection and qualifications; b. appointment of a substitute teacher from the RQA; c. experientail qualification for equitable promotion mechanism; d. termination for a just cause/after due process; e. conditions for consent for transfer; f. code of ethics; g. hiring/promotion based on academic and professional merit and fitness; h. conditions when professional licenses maybe revoked or invalidated; i. creation of independent research body to review teaching methods; j. additional compensation for off campus activities; k. special hardship, health and safety hazard allowances; l. order of preference in salary deduction; and m. health, wellness and medical benefits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-10-10

rows.author: I085;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE RELEASE OF 14TH MONTH PAY FOR ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS
rows.abstract: Seeks to further incentivize and motivate our public school teachers to improve work performance and productivity and at the same time alleviate their financial plights.  Proposes to grant a 14th month salary every year, in an amount equivalent to the 13th-month pay which shall be excluded from the computation of gross income provided the amount shall not exceed Eighty Two Thousand Pesos (82,000.00).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-10-10

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE POLICE LAW ENFORCEMENT COURTS, GRANTING THESE EXCLUSIVE ORIGINAL JURISDICTION OVER VIOLATIONS OF CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS AND PNP RULES OF ENGAGEMENT COMMITTED BY THE POLICE, AMENDING BATAS PAMBANSA BILANG 129, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"JUDICIARY REORGANIZATION ACT OF 1980\", APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFORE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Aims to prosecute rogue police elements through a special courts that will provide the public fair, impartial, and speedy disposition of complaints for violations of constitutional rights and PNP operational procedures and code of ethical standards. It shall handle all civil and criminal cases involving the abuse of authority of the members of the PNP including those arising out of the violation of its police operational procedures and other police protocols designed to protect the rights of the accused. Provides for periodic and continuing training program for the presiding judge and the court personnel of the police courts on police protocols, tactics and rules of engagement including Philippine and International Human Rights Law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2018-10-10

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN THE JURISDICTION AND POWER OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY OVER PETROLEUM PIPELINE OPERATIONS AND FOR THIS PURPOSE PROVIDE A PETROLEUM PIPELINE CODE TO PRESCRIBE STANDARDS FOR THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE AND ABANDONMENT OF LIQUID PETROLEUM PIPELINES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Intends to review, expand, improve, and promote regulations on our pipeline systems to ensure their safety and reliability and to provide the DOE the jurisdiction that will regulate, monitor, and oversee the operations of petroleum pipelines in the country.  Provides for the application for Concession under this Act to be filed with the Oil Industry Management Bureau (OIMB) of the DOE which shall examine and pass upon the same as well as upon the qualifications of the applicant.  Provides further that ownership, establishment, operation and maintenance of a pipeline shall be granted only to Filipino citizens or to corporations/associations organized under the laws of the Phils. at leas 60% of whose capital is owned by such citizens.
rows.status: Referred to Stakeholders on 2018-10-18

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE FARMERS AND FISHERFOLK ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM OF THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to capacitate our agricultural and fisher-folk communities through an enterprise development program that will provide assistance to farmers and fishermen in developing their own business through various opportunities to develop technical skills, use production equipment and facilities, gain access to credit, and avail of business development counselling services.  Proposes to establish a comprehensive and holistic approach in the formulation, coordination and implementation of enterprise development initiatives, consolidate the roles of different government agencies involved therein, intensify the building of entrepreneurship culture among farmers and fisherfolk, and provide incentives to private entities that support said initiatives of the government.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08857

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING A SYSTEM OF EXTENDING NO-COLLATERAL, LOW-INTEREST LOANS TO GRADUATES OF ANY COURSES OFFERED BY THE TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY OR DULY ACCREDITED LEARNING INSTITUTIONS WITH APPROVED OVERSEAS JOB CONTRACTS
rows.abstract: Proposes for a special loan granted to graduates of TESDA and other learning institutions credited by CHED with an approved overseas job contracts only. Aims to provide the much needed credit facility for our graduates, so that they may be able to afford the cost of pursuing employment overseas. Proposes to mandate all government and private banking and financial institutions to make the necessary provisions for extending such loans which shall be used exclusively for meeting said credit needs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2018-10-10

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SOCIAL SECURITY BENEFITS FOR BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND VOLUNTEER WORKERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Proposes to recognize the valuable services rendered by our barangay officials and volunteer workers by tapping the various government instrumentalities such as the GSIS, PAG-IBIG Fund, and PHILHEALTH. Provides for the mandatory membership and enrollment of all barangay officials and volunteers to the GSIS Life Insurance and Social Protection Program, including the PAGIBIG Fund Voluntary Membership Program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-10-10

rows.author: I088;I089;I077;I079;I091;I103;I096;I087;I102;I085;I086;I011;I092;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE CANCER CENTER, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Intends to oversee the continuity of the national program on cancer prevention and cure by creating an agency whose specific and primary focus is the advocacy of cancer awareness and treatment.  Enumerates several objectives of the PCC related to the following, among others: specialized cancer hospital; scientific research; publication/dissemination of the findings of researches on several aspects of cancer, its abnormalities and control; dissemination and exchange of ideas and information; training of medical personnel; studies of cellular anomalies; formation of other organization for a more effective programmatic approach; medical cancer services especially to the poor and less fortunate.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2018-10-10

rows.abstract: Seeks to require manufacturers precautionary labeling on household items which may contain substances that are considered toxic, corrosive, harmful irritants, strong sensitizers or flammable through a standard of signage and symbols that would alert the consumer of the potential hazards
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2018-10-10

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING THE PHILIPPINE FILM INDUSTRY THROUGH AN ANNUAL FILM QUOTA AND OTHER SUPPORT MEASURES
rows.abstract: Aims to safeguard the artistic and economic development of the film industry through an annual film quota that will require all cinemas and theatrical venues to exhibit only Filipino films for a period of twenty eight (28) days , from June 1 to June 14 and from December 18 to December 31. Seeks to guarantee all Filipino films a full week's run in all commercial theatres and booking priority on \"payday playdates\".
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2018-10-10

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE GRANT OF STUDENT FARE DISCOUNT PRIVILEGES ON PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to institutionalize the twenty percent (20%) discount granted to students in various public land tranportation which includes, but not limited to, PUBs, PUJs, taxis, tricycles, Transport Network Vehicle Services (TNVS), Trasport Network Companies (TNCs), shuttle services, and public and private railways such as the LRT, MRT, AND PNR. Provides that in the case of air transportation utilities, the discount shall only apply to the base fare or the price of the ticket before taxes and costs for ancillary services. Proposes further that Filipino students who will travel abroad for education, training, and competition shall be exempts from the payment of travel tax.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08885

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE BARANGAYS THROUGH SUPPORT FOR BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND VOLUNTEER WORKERS
rows.abstract: Intends to ensure that the people working in the barangay level are highly-motivated, effective, and capable in the planning and implementation of local projects and programs. Proposes to properly compensate and reward them for quality performance, and promote constant appraisal of their skills by providing other incentives and benefits such as honorarium, trainings and workshops, PhilHealth and free legal services for barangay health workers, barangay tanods, barangay officials and volunteer workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-10-10

rows.author: I044;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish the Department of Overseas Filipino Workers to be the single government agency that would provide a unified and coordinated service OFWs from deployment and repatriation. DOFW shall prepare, integrate, coordinate, supervise, and control all plans, programs, projects, and activities of the Government relative to overseas employment.
Provides for a Special Assistance Fund for OFWs in distress in the amount of One Billion Pesos.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE FISCAL REGIME FOR THE MINING INDUSTRY
rows.title_short: Establishing The Fiscal Regime For The Mining Industry
rows.abstract:
Seeks to impose tax on the following: a margin -based royalty tax on large-scale metallic and non-metallic mining operations outside of mineral reservations from 1% to 5%; three percent (3%) royalty tax for mining contractors of large-scale metallic and non-metallic within mineral reservations ; one-tenth (1/10) of one percent (1%) of gross output for mining contractors of small-scale metallic and non-metallic within or outside mineral reservations; a margin-based windfall profits tax on income from mining operations before corporate income tax from 1% to 10% for each taxable year.

Requires small-scale miners to register with the Mining Board of the concerned local government unit and with the Mines and Geoscience Bureau (MGB) and may organize themselves into cooperatives in order to qualify for the awarding of a people´s small-scale mining contract.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2018-11-12, transmitted to the Senate on 2018-11-13 and received by the Senate on 2018-11-13

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO ALL INDIGENT FILIPINOS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CHAPTER 5, TITLE III, BOOK IV OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987\", APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
\"Hustisya Para sa Lahat Act of 2018\"
Intends to adjust the parameters currently being used by the Public Attorney's Office (PAO)in qualifying indigent persons.

Defines \"indigent\" as any individual who falls into any of the following categories:
a) whose net income falls below the most recent official poverty threshold by the Phil. Statistics Authority (PSA);
b) those identified as poor and near poor based on National Household Targeting System (NHTS); or
c) those vulnerable households who are living under precarious circumstances (members of the informal economy/sectors, Indigenous Peoples, and those living in geographically isolated and 
disadvantaged areas.
